newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-REAL BETIS HOPING TO DEFY THE ODDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-REAL BETIS HOPING TO DEFY THE ODDS.

text.p: The Spanish Cup has a unique place in the hearts of the country's soccer fans.

For 26 years after the inaugural Cup in 1902, it was the only opportunity for clubs from disparate parts of the country to play against each other, and excercise regional rivalries, until the national league started in 1928.
The first final was contested in Madrid between Basque club Vizcaya and modern-day giants Barcelona.
Vizcaya triumphed 1-0 -- their only victory -- and have since disappeared into obscurity.
By contrast, the Catalans have gone on to create their own niche in Spanish Cup history, winning 22 times.
The first eight Cup finals were held in Madrid, much to the resentment of clubs in other parts of the country.
Not surprisingly, Madrid FC, later to become Real Madrid, managed to take the honours four times in those early years.
The first Cup final to be held outside Madrid was in 1910 when the all-Basque clash between Athletic Bilbao and San Sebastian was staged in the latter club's home city.
In a country without a national stadium, it created a precedent for moving the final around Spain.
Last year's final was held in Zaragoza. The showpiece has also been staged in Barcelona, Valladolid and Valencia.
Madrid, having staged the Cup final 33 times since 1957, remains the main venue.

The Cup has been fought for almost continuously since 1902. It was contested throughout World War Two and the only interuptions in its 95-year history were the cancellation of the 1937 and 1938 finals because of the Spanish Civil War.
Two clubs have won by five-goal margins. Athletic Bilbao beat Madrid FC 5-0 in 1915 while in 1980 Real Madrid thrashed Castilla, their reserve team now known as Real Madrid B, 6-1.
Sevilla managed to put six goals past Racing de Ferrol to win 6-2 in 1939, which still remains the highest-scoring final.
Athletic Bilbao are the most successful team in Cup history with a record 23 victories, a feat Barcelona will equal if they win on Saturday.
Athletic Bilbao striker Telmo Zarra remains the most prolific scorer in Cup final history with eight goals in seven final appearences between 1943 and 1955.
Zarra is also the only man to score four times in a final. He scored all his side's goals in the 4-1 win over Vallidolid in 1950.
Despite their status as one of the heavyweights of Spanish soccer, Barcelona have also found winning the Cup beyond them in recent years.
They last won in 1990 when they beat Real Madrid 2-0.
Real Betis fans have to delve much deeper into their memories to recall their club's solitary victory in 1977.
The Seville club have appeared in only one other final, in 1931.
